newsitem.title: BENIN: Benin enacts tough law to restrain private media.
newsitem.headline: Benin enacts tough law to restrain private media.

text.p: Benin's parliament adopted a new law allowing private ownership of radio and television stations but setting a heavy penalty for libel, lawmakers said on Sunday.

Under the new law, insulting the West African country's president, foreign heads of state and foreign ministers is punishable by up to five years in prison or a fine of up to 10 million CFA francs ($17,700).
People accused of libel or defamation have one week to produce proof of their allegation but courts will not entertain evidence that is more than 10 years old.
Local press groups lobbied unsuccessfully against the law before deputies voted for it overwhelmingly on Friday night.
The bill also sets up the High Council for Communications with authority to issue private broadcast licences -- five years for radio and 10 for television.
